steps.title: How to become a Canadian citizen
steps.subtitle: Adults and minor children · apply online
steps.stat.feeMinorNote: Under 18 · no right of citizenship fee
steps.stat.timeSnapshot: As of {date}. It may have changed.
steps.stat.daysNote: In the 5 years before you apply
steps.stat.daysNoteMinor: With a Canadian parent or a parent applying at the same time. Otherwise, {days} days.
steps.family.title: Fees for your family
steps.family.note: Pay online when you’re ready to submit, then upload the receipt. If an adult isn’t approved, the {right} right of citizenship fee is refunded.
steps.family.noteMinors: Pay online when you’re ready to submit, then upload the receipt. Children under 18 don’t pay the {right} right of citizenship fee.
steps.age.label: Age on the day you sign
steps.journey.title: The steps
steps.step.check.title: Check you’re eligible
steps.step.check.detail: Permanent resident, 1,095 days in Canada in the last 5 years, taxes filed for 3 of those years if you had to.
steps.step.check.detailMinor: A parent or guardian applies for a child under 18. With a Canadian parent or a parent applying at the same time, no minimum days are needed.
steps.step.apply.title: Apply online
steps.step.apply.detail: Create your account, calculate your days, pay the fee and upload documents. Families and groups can apply together.
steps.step.apply.detailMinor: A parent or guardian creates the account, fills out the child’s form, pays the fee and uploads documents. Families can apply together.
steps.step.aor.title: Get your acknowledgement of receipt
steps.step.aor.detail: A confirmation email comes first. The AOR follows once your application is complete, and then you can check your status online.
steps.step.test.title: Take the citizenship test
steps.step.test.detail: Invitation within a few weeks or months. 20 questions, 45 minutes, online, with 30 days to take it.
steps.step.interview.title: Interview, if needed
steps.step.interview.detail: An official may meet you to confirm your identity, check your original documents and verify you’re eligible.
steps.step.ceremony.title: Take the oath at a ceremony
steps.step.ceremony.detail: You’re invited at least 1 week ahead, in person or online. It’s the last step: you become a citizen when you take the oath.
steps.step.ceremony.detailMinor: Children {min} to 17 take the oath at the ceremony. Children under {min} don’t need to take it.
steps.step.passport.title: Get your certificate, then a passport
steps.step.passport.detail: Your PR card is cut or collected at the ceremony. Apply for a passport once you have your citizenship certificate.
steps.language: Between 18 and 54? Send proof of English or French at CLB/NCLC level 4 with your application.
steps.noTest: {age, select, minor {Children under 18} other {Adults 55 and older}} don’t take the test or prove language skills.
steps.alreadyBody: Check your application status online. It shows each step, from the test to the ceremony.
steps.returned: Sign and date your application the same day you calculate your days, and send it soon: IRCC returns applications received more than 90 days after the signature date.
steps.returnedMinor: Send the application soon after it’s signed and dated: IRCC returns applications received more than 90 days after the signature date.
steps.handoffNote: You’ll create an account on IRCC’s citizenship application site to apply and pay.
ceremony.title: Citizenship ceremony and oath
ceremony.subtitle: Practise the oath · what to bring · what comes next
ceremony.loading: Preparing the oath and ceremony guide
ceremony.oath.title: The oath of citizenship
ceremony.oath.done: That’s the whole oath. You’re ready.
ceremony.oath.tip: At the ceremony, you repeat each line after the presiding official. Say it in both official languages if you can.
ceremony.oath.tipSwear: At the ceremony, you repeat each line after the presiding official. Say it in both official languages if you can. Bring a holy book if you want to swear on one.
ceremony.day.title: On the day
ceremony.day.ip.1.title: Register
ceremony.day.ip.1.detail: An official checks your ID and asks a few questions, and collects your PR card and signed consent form.
ceremony.day.ip.2.title: Take the oath
ceremony.day.ip.2.detail: Stand if you can for the oath and O Canada. Over 100 people may take the oath with you.
ceremony.day.ip.3.title: Sign the oath form
ceremony.day.ip.3.detail: Signing confirms you took the oath. If you asked for a paper certificate, you get it at the ceremony.
ceremony.day.v.1.title: Join with the link in your invitation
ceremony.day.v.1.detail: Use your seat number as your screen name. At large ceremonies you may wait up to 30 minutes to be let in.
ceremony.day.v.2.title: Private registration
ceremony.day.v.2.detail: An official checks your ID, asks a few questions and watches you cut your PR card.
ceremony.day.v.3.title: Take the oath, then sign the form
ceremony.day.v.3.detail: Stay seated and on camera. Sign the Oath or Affirmation form that same day and send it back as the invitation explains.
ceremony.day.length: Ceremonies last a few hours. Check your invitation for the arrival time.
ceremony.bring.title: What to bring
ceremony.bring.invitation.title: Your ceremony invitation
ceremony.bring.invitation.detail: It arrives at least 1 week before, by email if you gave one.
ceremony.bring.prCard.title: Your PR card, even if it’s expired
ceremony.bring.prCard.detail: Or your Confirmation of Permanent Residence (IMM 5292 or IMM 5688).
ceremony.bring.landing.title: Your Record of Landing (IMM 1000), if you have one
ceremony.bring.landing.detail: Only if you became a permanent resident before June 28, 2002 and still have the document.
ceremony.bring.ids.title: 2 pieces of ID
ceremony.bring.ids.detail: Adults: at least 1 with your photo and signature, like a driver’s licence or passport.
ceremony.bring.form.title: The signed consent form
ceremony.bring.form.detail: The permission release and consent form in your invitation.
ceremony.bring.form.detailVirtual: The permission release and consent form, if your invitation includes one.
ceremony.bring.seat.title: Your virtual seat number
ceremony.bring.seat.detail: It’s on the first page of your invitation.
ceremony.bring.scissors.title: A pair of scissors
ceremony.bring.scissors.detail: You’ll cut your PR card at the start of the ceremony.
ceremony.bring.book.title: A holy book, if you like
ceremony.bring.book.detail: Optional, if you want to swear the oath on one.
ceremony.after.title: After you’re a citizen
ceremony.after.cert.title: Citizenship certificate
ceremony.after.cert.detail: E-certificate in the IRCC Portal within 5 business days of your signed oath form. Paper: at an in-person ceremony, or by mail 2 to 4 weeks after a virtual one.
ceremony.after.passport.title: Passport before you travel
ceremony.after.passport.detail: Your PR card is gone and a certificate isn’t a travel document. Apply for a passport once you have your certificate.
ceremony.after.vote.title: Register to vote
ceremony.after.vote.detail: Voting is a right and a responsibility of every citizen 18 and older.
ceremony.handoffNote: On canada.ca: rescheduling, guests, what to wear and the anthem.
